title: Ledger acknowledgement precedes durable memory-state mutation without recovery
evidence: revoke_record commits MEMORY_RECORD_REVOKED through append_event before opening the mutation transaction at 663. Ledger append commits independently (cortex_persist_ledger.py:257-271); engine constructor only initializes schema, without projection replay. add_record and retract_attribution use the same pattern.
trigger: Process stops or the second database transaction fails after ledger append succeeds and before memory updates commit.
impact: A durable revocation receipt can coexist with an ACTIVE readable record after reopening; committed additions can lack their memory projection. No runtime execution was performed.

title: Revocation silently truncates dependency closure after 1024 levels
evidence: Recursive closure uses c.depth < 1024; add_record accepts arbitrarily deep acyclic dependency chains. The returned total_invalidated does not signal truncation. Retraction has the same bound at 1062-1075.
trigger: Create an acyclic dependency chain deeper than 1024 and revoke its root.
impact: Nodes beyond the bound remain ACTIVE and retain their blobs; advertised transitive revocation is incomplete.

title: Policy epoch rolls back on engine restart
evidence: __init__ unconditionally initializes _host_epoch to 1; advance_policy_epoch (333-340) updates only this instance field. add_record signs and records using that field, while get_record accepts stored epoch without comparing a persistent host minimum.
trigger: Advance epoch above 1, reopen MemoryGovernanceEngine on the same database, register principal key, then create a record.
impact: New records are issued under epoch 1 despite previously advancing the authoritative epoch, contradicting monotonic policy governance.

title: Concurrent publish can overwrite the fail-stop state
evidence: publish admits RUNNING->WRITING at 82, then unconditionally stores RUNNING at 91; epistemic_halt independently stores HALTING at 123. Identical content exists in the assigned workspace skill-library copy.
trigger: epistemic_halt runs after publish admission and before its final status store.
impact: The example resumes RUNNING after a halt and may leave an odd sequence, contradicting its irreversible fail-stop guarantee. This is an example defect; no production consumer was established.

title: Retry exhaustion does not perform the documented halt
evidence: Line 38 specifies invoking epistemic_halt and POISONED after MAX_RETRIES; read instead returns None at 119 without changing status. The workspace skill-library copy is identical.
trigger: A reader reaches MAX_RETRIES while a writer is stalled or contention persists.
impact: Implementations copied from this canonical example silently abandon a read while remaining non-poisoned, failing the documented fail-stop contract.

title: Falsifiability acceptance is disabled by optimized Python
evidence: delta > falsifiability_threshold is enforced only by assert (218-220); success is logged unconditionally afterwards (222).
trigger: Launch CLI using python -O with a nonempty graph and drivers whose measured delta fails threshold.
impact: Rejected simulations instead finish successfully and are described as suitable for in-vitro follow-up.

title: Selecting therapy targets from a set makes pipeline nondeterministic
evidence: get_structural_driver_nodes returns list(set(G.nodes()) - matched_in_nodes); execute_pipeline selects drivers[:3] at 205-207.
trigger: Same input has more than three unmatched string nodes and Python hash randomization differs across processes.
impact: Therapy targets and resulting delta can vary for identical input, contradicting the deterministic pipeline contract.

title: IFC parser splits semicolons inside quoted values
evidence: current_statement.split(';') has no quote state; comment stripping likewise uses trimmed.find("/*") regardless of quoting.
trigger: A valid IFC string property contains a semicolon or /*.
impact: Entities are silently lost or corrupted while parse returns Ok, affecting extracted compliance data.

title: Setback distance fabricated from local placement axes
evidence: SetbackDistance is populated as min(abs(x), abs(y)) from local placement without property boundary geometry or parent placement composition.
trigger: Building has a translated/rotated parent placement or parcel boundary unrelated to the local axes.
impact: A synthetic numeric setback is exposed as an actual property and can yield incorrect spatial compliance conclusions.

title: Conformity simulator authorizes CE marking even when checks fail
evidence: overall_status at line 148 depends on all_passed, but market_access_declaration is unconditionally CE_MARKING_AUTHORIZED at line 149; audit_sitrep returns False when SITREP is absent (49-51), and generate_annex_vi_pack still writes the declaration (164-165).
trigger: Run this explicitly labelled simulator with a missing SITREP or any failing checklist.
impact: The generated example declaration asserts authorization while recording NON_CONFORMANT, creating a contradictory output that cannot support the claimed marking. This is an example artifact issue, not evidence of a production legal approval flow.

title: Conformity example labels a status string as verified hardware evidence
evidence: Lines 82-87 check only whether ROOT-named tasks have attestation.status == ATTESTED_BY_OPERATOR. No signature, trusted key or payload binding is checked; line 95 nevertheless emits Hardware (Secure Enclave P-256) validada, and line 96 takes a signature substring without verification.
trigger: Provide a SITREP ROOT task with the expected status string and an arbitrary or absent signature.
impact: The example marks human-supervision evidence PASS and claims validated hardware without authenticating any evidence. Simulator labeling limits the scope but does not make that evidence statement accurate.

title: Authenticate tenant selection in the multi-tenant example
evidence: fetch reads X-Tenant-ID directly and selects env[`TENANT_${tenantId}`] before SELECT * FROM records; no authenticated principal or tenant authorization is checked.
trigger: Deploy the illustrated handler with multiple tenant bindings and send another tenant identifier in the header.
impact: The example permits callers to select another tenant database and retrieve its records. This is an example defect, not evidence that any deployed service uses it.

title: Normalize session expiry before comparing SQLite timestamps
evidence: createSession stores new Date(...).toISOString() (line 98); validateSession compares expires_at > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP lexically (line 103).
trigger: Validate an expired session later on the same UTC calendar day as its ISO-formatted expiry.
impact: The T separator sorts after the space in SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, so expired sessions can remain accepted until the UTC date changes.

title: F60 numerator can overflow before applying the advertised score cap
evidence: Five unconstrained u64 parameters are multiplied into u128 at 144-148; final cap is applied only at 157.
trigger: Call public compute_score_f60 with g=l=a=b=p=100000000 (100 in F60 units): product is 10^40, above u128 capacity.
impact: Debug builds panic; release builds wrap and may return an incorrect bounded score rather than saturating at 1000. No production caller found in targeted references.

title: ZCA whitening crashes for a valid single-feature matrix
evidence: The guard allows shape (n,1) for n>=2; np.cov(..., rowvar=False) produces a scalar covariance and the code passes it directly to np.linalg.eigh. The PC1 helper in the same file explicitly handles scalar covariance.
trigger: Call compute_zca_whitening with shape (2,1), or compute_whitened_cka with either input having one feature.
impact: Raises a dimensionality error rather than returning whitened representations.

title: Malformed tool arguments terminate the stdio server
evidence: process_request invokes handler(params) without exception handling; run_stdio lines 1454-1461 also has no exception boundary. _tool_query_ledger converts an arbitrary string limit using int() at lines 1009-1010; _read_message calls json.loads at line 613 without a parse-error handler.
trigger: Send tools/call for bft_query_ledger with arguments.limit="invalid", or send malformed JSON over the connected stdio transport.
impact: An input validation error escapes the main loop and kills the MCP process, interrupting subsequent legitimate requests instead of returning a per-request error.

title: Malformed action fields raise instead of returning rejection
evidence: Lines 47–51 call int on untrusted payload values, but the handler at line 55 catches only ValueError and KeyError. int(None) and int([]) raise TypeError.
trigger: Call verify_payload with both action_class and agent_id present and agent_id=None (or a numeric field containing a list), using an otherwise recognized action class.
impact: The boolean verification API propagates an exception rather than returning False; consumers expecting deterministic rejection can fail a request/task. No protected-effect consumer or authorization bypass was established.

title: Check arithmetic overflow at the C ABI boundary
evidence: b60_sexa_add performs f1 + f2 and s1 + s2 + carry as unchecked u64 additions and returns 0; API accepts arbitrary u64 arguments with no numeric preconditions.
trigger: For example s1=u64::MAX, s2=1 with valid output pointers.
impact: Release arithmetic can wrap while reporting exact addition success; overflow-checked builds panic across extern C and may abort the embedding process.

title: Missing Lean oracle is replaced by a numeric heuristic certification
evidence: Missing oracle or launch failure restores Beta when bkm_acc.lower_bound() >= 3600 and gamma agrees (also lines123-125); final output claims native Lean reflection.
trigger: Run example with missing/unlaunchable oracle and threshold-satisfying scenario.
impact: Example can report SingularityCandidateIsolated and native verification without running the formal oracle. This is example evidence, not demonstrated production authorization bypass.

title: Trace validator ignores sequence continuity and incomplete writes
evidence: validateTransition names _currentSeq but never reads it; only checks parity/write boolean (19-32). isValidTrace [] returns true even when inWrite=true (36).
trigger: Validate a single WriteBegin with odd seq, or WriteBegin 3 followed by WriteEnd 2, starting at (0,false).
impact: The example validator accepts unfinished or regressing traces despite its seqlock validation wording. Its two concrete decide proofs do not cover these cases or prove runtime seqlock correctness.

title: SHM example requests writable ctypes buffer from read-only mmap
evidence: mmap uses ACCESS_READ immediately before Kudurru64.from_buffer(mm), which requires a writable buffer.
trigger: Run this isolated PoC on the supplied 64-byte fixture.
impact: The demo fails before reading or printing its fields; its zero-copy demonstration cannot work as written.

title: Master ledger explicitly selects NORMAL durability despite FULL requirement
evidence: BFTMasterLedgerWAL sets PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL at 112, immediately below comments requiring FULL for a master ledger at 110-111; .babylon60rules requires synchronous FULL.
trigger: Use this ledger class for committed transactions and suffer OS/power failure before WAL synchronization.
impact: The configured durability is weaker than the class contract and committed recent transactions may be lost; no crash experiment was run.

title: Version synchronization reports success for missing required targets
evidence: check_or_update_file returns False for missing files or unmatched patterns (37–44); sync_all only returns failure for drift_detected when dry_run is true (133–139).
trigger: Run --sync when a required target is absent or its version pattern has changed.
impact: Script prints that all surfaces are aligned and exits zero although a required surface was never synchronized.

title: Unique query generator inevitably stops making progress
evidence: Both query length and word indices depend exclusively on len(unique_queries); length cycles mod 6 and vocabulary indices mod len(VOCAB).
trigger: Execute the 1000-query benchmark.
impact: The candidate repeats after at most lcm(6,len(VOCAB)) distinct lengths/offsets, fewer than 1000 here. On the first duplicate set size freezes and the while loop repeats forever before inference.

title: Host triage emits static corpus observations as current audit results
evidence: Workers select static AUDIT_CORPUS entries and add trigonometric jitter at lines 79–86; output at 128–148 describes a completed workstation triage with findings and measured-looking scores, without reading the host.
trigger: Run the script on a changed or unrelated host.
impact: The saved report presents stale constants and synthesized metrics as host findings and may prompt inappropriate remediation. No host runtime state is inferred here.

title: Concurrent seqlock test never validates payload consistency
evidence: Reader extracts seq,cid,aid,phash,flags but only checks seq parity at 62; writer encodes w independently into cluster_id,agent_id and payload at 77–78.
trigger: A channel returns an even sequence paired with mixed fields from two writes.
impact: The torn-read regression reports zero failures despite an inconsistent snapshot; claimed absence of torn reads is not tested.

title: Turnstile Worker example references an undeclared env binding
evidence: The standalone export defines async fetch(request) but its JSON request body evaluates env.TURNSTILE_SECRET at line 55; the example declares no env parameter or enclosing env binding.
trigger: Copy the provided module Worker validation example and submit a form.
impact: Evaluating the validation request body raises ReferenceError instead of calling siteverify; the required server validation example does not work as written.

title: Single-chunk ledger example accepts an invalid chunk
evidence: verifyLedgerStream returns true for [_] regardless of deltaValid; only the two-or-more branch calls verifyChunkBoundary, which checks validity.
trigger: Apply the canonical example to a singleton Chunk with deltaValid=false.
impact: The documented verifier accepts a ledger explicitly marked invalid. This is an example defect; no production consumer or deployed bypass is asserted.

title: Repository inventory falsely marks every repository as having a README
evidence: GraphQL requests workflows but never a README object; enrichment nevertheless writes has_readme=True unconditionally.
trigger: A queried repository lacks a README.
impact: Downstream repository audits are given a false positive for documentation presence and can skip needed remediation.
